title: Bridging Research Gaps Between Academic Research and Legal Investigations of Algorithmic Discrimination

bias_targets.methodology: Analysis of civil enforcement actions, lawsuits, and regulatory settlements involving algorithms alleged to have disparate impacts on racial and ethnic minorities across domains like tenant screening, facial recognition, credit scoring, and targeted advertising.

Review of legal complaints and settlements concerning algorithms alleged to discriminate based on sex or gender in areas such as automated recruiting, targeted ad delivery, and credit limit determinations.
Examination of civil lawsuits and EEOC complaints involving alleged age discrimination in automated recruiting software, job application screening tools, and ad-delivery algorithms.
Review of enforcement actions involving algorithmic tenant screening programs and credit scores alleged to disproportionately harm low-income applicants and housing voucher recipients.
Identification and analysis of legal cases alleging disability discrimination in automated job application screening tools and residency match algorithms.
Review of civil lawsuits alleging algorithmic discrimination based on national origin, such as in psychiatry residency matching algorithms.
Review of civil lawsuits alleging algorithmic discrimination based on religion, specifically within the context of a residency training match algorithm.
